title: Prompt - Unique Ground Truth (UGT)
questionDescription:
The prompts are open-ended in this project, so there cannot be one possible response to the user (For example, wording can differ), BUT it should not be the case that the prompt leads to distinct outcomes. It’s okay if there’s multiple possible paths the agent could take to arrive at the answer, but the key points in the answer, as requested in the prompt, should be the same.

Please be extra vigilant in checking this dimension as we want to provide more visibility regarding these potential issues! (That’s not to say to apply this more liberally, per se, but rather a reminder to keep this possibility in mind.)

 Note: Conflicting information related to a prompt request does not necessarily mean that [Multiple Valid Answers] applies. If one source is clearly more authoritative or up to date, it should be considered the fixed choice for consideration/inclusion in the answer. If both sources are equally credible and nothing resolves the conflict, then it should fail for [Multiple Valid Answers]. 

 Note: Disagreement between models is not definitive proof of [Multiple Valid Answers] - the determination should be made on the basis of evidence in the prompt and environment. 


CHECK THE SPEC FOR ADDITIONAL NOTES
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Multiple Valid Answers] 
- The prompt can reasonably produce two or more different correct answers (even if a leading interpretation exists), and the prompt does not clearly indicate which answer is intended and the ambiguity cannot be resolved by referencing the environment for additional context (e.g., a documented convention exists clarifying an unclear instruction).
The prompt has a unique ground truth answer. All the experts on the subject would come to the same conclusion

title: Prompt - Feasibility
questionDescription:
The project now has a Persona ACL (Access control list). For some services, the agent can ONLY access records that are owned by, shared with, or otherwise visible to the assigned persona. 

Note that the universe explorer by default shows ALL records (even those that shouldn't be seen by the current persona) - make your determination of whether the current user has access to a particular record by examining its details based on the service in question (e.g., for an email, see if they're the sender, recipient, or cc'd, for slack, see if they're in the channel in question, and so on).

Read actions are persona-scoped in 7 services - Gmail, Slack, GCal, and the Drive-family (GDrive/GDocs/GSheets/GSlides, which inherit Drive's file ACL). The agent only sees records owned by / shared with / visible to that persona. 
Reads are unscoped in the other 6 - Contacts, GitHub, Snowflake, Trello, Linear, Confluence (shared across personas).

Write actions are not blocked by ACL at all.

title: Prompt - Contrived / Unnatural Prompts
questionDescription:
This should check for artificial difficulty vs. natural complexity.

Prompts should read as realistic human workplace requests.
Exact titles and values are fine when they are naturally human-readable (e.g., "GEOGAMES_SPEC.docx").
Penalize the mention of unnatural opaque IDs, generated filenames, full agent IDs, or similar references when they're not actually necessary. (E.g., "geogames_spec_23mf2ldf02lfasdlov23rmfmmfmm234.docx")

Contrived examples include:
- demanding exact timestamps ("Find the email from January 15th at 3:47 PM")
- requiring arbitrary format constraints ("Respond in exactly 3 sentences using passive voice")
- asking the agent to do something no real employee would do ("Intentionally send an incorrect email to test error handling").

Natural difficulty comes from entity confusion, scattered information, conflicting data across services, and hidden root causes. Prompts written as step-by-step command lists ("First search emails, then check CRM…") should also be considered contrived.

Prompts such as riddles that are intentionally constraints/details laden should not be considered contrived.

title: Prompt - Truthfulness
questionDescription:
How to classify a naming/identifier error as major or minor:
- Major: errors in tight identifiers—channel names, document IDs, JE IDs, vendor or company entity names, account numbers, dollar amounts, dates, fiscal periods, ticket/issue IDs. These are passed literally into tool calls and don't tolerate near-matches.



- Minor: errors in loose descriptors—person first-name only references where the universe context disambiguates, role titles, casual entity references. These tolerate natural language.



- Escalation rule: a "minor" error escalates to "major" if it actually causes agent failure (e.g., wrong first name in a universe where two people share it).

title: Universe - Cross-service Coherence
questionDescription:
See the table in Appendix - Universe Inconsistency Examples for examples of each error, and see the Examples & Notes section for this error for further guidance. 
Note: This error applies to synthetic data - consult the list below for what data in the universe(s) used in this project are synthetic:
HarmonyGames: snowflake and confluence data
This dimension flags universe inconsistencies directly, independent of whether they caused an agent failure. Note that this dimension does not require that the inconsistency leads to an agent failure, nor is it focused specifically on cb-introduced changes — it fails based on the presence of the inconsistency itself, because these defects silently corrupt the storyline and often surface only after tasking is complete. If you notice knock-on effects to other universe data, or that a specific inconsistency is part of a larger pattern, please also note this in your feedback (alongside any relevant evidence).

Auditors must perform a VISUAL, per-artifact review of the universe data touched by the task (Universe Explorer / Sandbox). Check within each artifact and across the fields of related artifacts and services for the following:
TEMPORAL CONSISTENCY — Do date-bearing fields agree with each other within the same artifact and with 'today's' date? (e.g., an invoice booked with TxnDate 2026-05-13 whose description/memo references 'October 2026', or a May invoice assessing an October late fee.)
SEMANTIC / CATEGORY CONSISTENCY — Do categorical fields match the described work or entity, including naming? (e.g., a line item described as 'Roof repair' categorized as 'Drywall / Water-Damage Repair'; a single 'Monthly management fee' charge mapping to three different items; overlapping names that create ambiguity within the universe.)
CROSS-SERVICE REFERENTIAL CONSISTENCY — Is the same entity/fact represented consistently across services, and do references resolve? (e.g., a name spelled/keyed differently in email vs CRM; a Linear ticket referencing an Airtable record that does not exist; a foreign key with no matching entity.)
QUANTITATIVE / RECONCILIATION CONSISTENCY — Do numeric fields reconcile? (e.g., line items that do not sum to the stated invoice total; balances/aggregates that do not match the underlying transactions.)
STATE / LIFECYCLE CONSISTENCY — Do status/lifecycle fields agree with the record's activity? (e.g., a ticket marked 'Closed' that has later activity; a lease marked 'Terminated' that still collects rent; an invoice marked 'Paid' with no payment record.)
IDENTIFIER / UNIQUENESS / FORMAT CONSISTENCY — Are identifiers well-formed, non-null, unique where required, and following a single consistent scheme within a service? (e.g., DocNumber mixing INV-RM-0001, 2026-WO-114, BILL-2026-119, plain '2254', and a null value; BILL- prefixes on customer invoices; two records sharing an ID that should be unique; customer IDs mixing numeric '101' and 'proj-<hash>'.)
OTHER — Any other internal inconsistency that does not fit the categories above; the auditor must describe it in the justification.

[Fail – Temporal Field Inconsistency] — One or more date-bearing fields within an artifact contradict each other or "today's" date (e.g., description/memo period does not match TxnDate; a booking assesses a charge for a future period).
• The fixed date for the v2.1 universe is Apr 26, 2026
• The fixed date for the v2.2 universe is Apr 28, 2026
• The fixed date for the v3 universe is Jun 12, 2026
• The fixed date for the v4 universe is July 01, 2026

[Fail – Semantic / Category Inconsistency] — A categorical or descriptive field does not match the underlying work/entity, the same real-world charge/entity is categorized inconsistently across artifacts, or names overlap in a way that creates ambiguity.

[Fail – Cross-service Referential Inconsistency] — The same entity/fact is represented inconsistently across services, or a reference does not resolve (e.g., a name keyed differently in email vs CRM; an entity referenced in one service but absent in another when required; a broken/dangling foreign key).

[Fail – Quantitative / Reconciliation Inconsistency] — Numeric fields do not reconcile (e.g., line items do not sum to the stated total; balances or aggregate figures do not match the underlying transactions/records).

[Fail – State / Lifecycle Inconsistency] — A status/lifecycle field contradicts the record's activity or related records (e.g., a ticket marked "Closed" with later activity; a lease marked "Terminated" that still collects rent; an invoice marked "Paid" with no payment record).

[Fail – Other Universe Inconsistency] — Any other internal inconsistency that does not fit the categories above. Describe the inconsistency, the artifacts/fields involved, and why it breaks consistency in the justification.

[Non-Fail – Minor Universe Inconsistency] — A single, low-impact inconsistency that does not affect solvability or storyline coherence (e.g., a purely cosmetic ID-format variation that is plausibly intentional and consistently applied).

The universe data is internally consistent: dates agree with each other and with "today's" date; categorical fields match the described work/entities; the same entity is represented consistently across services and all references resolve; numeric fields reconcile; status/lifecycle fields match activity; and identifiers are well-formed, unique, and follow a consistent scheme within each service.

title: Rubrics - All-Failing Rubrics
questionDescription:
After rubric verifiers run, CBs are required to review any rubric that failed all completed runs (namely “All-failing” rubrics or AF rubrics) and add a 1–2 line justification confirming the failure is a genuine model failure and not a rubric quality issue. "All completed runs" means only runs that finished without an error — if 4 of 6 completed, the rubric must have failed all 4. If none of the rubrics failed all completed runs, this step is empty and no justification is needed.



In some tasks, this will be in a text box at the end of the rubric run step and in most new tasks (this is the format we're backfilling tasks to), this will be in the rubric rating step at the end of the verifier runs. 



IMPORTANT: If no AF rubrics exist, this dimension doesn't need to be audited.

Two or more all-failing rubrics have a quality issue that causes the failure — e.g., fictional tool name, overly specific wording, beyond prompt scope, unfairly penalizes a valid agent approach, or not grounded in GT. The CB either did not notice the rubric problem or provided a justification that inadvertently reveals it. This indicates a false negative — the task may appear harder than it is due to a bad rubric.

[Non-Fail - Poor All-Fail Rubric Justification]

[Non-Fail - One Invalid All-Fail Rubric]

This indicates a false negative — the task may appear harder than it is due to a bad rubric.



(Note: There may be more all-failing rubrics, but only one of them has to have a quality issue for the non-fail to apply. If more all-failing rubrics have quality issues that cause failure, then the task fails)

All rubrics that failed all completed runs are valid — self-contained, grounded in GT, within prompt scope, and using real tools. The CB's justifications confirm the failures reflect genuine model reasoning or execution gaps, not rubric artifacts. If no rubrics failed all completed runs, this dimension is automatically a 5.

title: Trajectory - Failure Signature Concentration
questionDescription:
A failure signature = the exact set of rubrics a rollout failed. Need >=2 distinct signatures and no single signature >50% of failing rollouts (exactly 50% OK).

Two failing rollouts count as different patterns only when they differ on at least 2 rubric results.

Example:
R1 fails: 2, 4, 6
R2 fails: 4, 6, 8
R3 fails: 2, 4, 6
R4 fails: 4, 6, 8
R5 fails: 4, 6, 8
R6 fails: 2, 4, 6
There are two distinct patterns here since these rollouts differ on both C2 and C8.

R1 fails: 2, 4, 6
R2 fails: 4, 6
R3 fails: 2, 4, 6
R4 fails: 4, 6
R5 fails: 4, 6
R6 fails: 2, 4, 6
There's only a single distinct pattern here as the difference only revolves around a single criterion: C2.

Additionally, no set of failing criteria should be over-represented in the runs (even if ultimately there are enough distinct sets) - this is checked against a 50% threshold. So if R1-4 all missed only C1, even if R5-6 are distinct, this is still failing.
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Too Few Signatures]
Fewer than 2 distinct patterns across failing rollouts.

[Fail - Signature Over-Concentrated]
One signature accounts for >50% of failing rollouts.
>=2 distinct signatures and none exceeds 50%.

title: Trajectory - Error Rate
questionDescription:
Sometimes, runs may error out. CBs are allowed to continue as long as there are at least 4 successful runs (i.e., max of 2 erroneous runs). This is not the same as a “run with rubric failures”.



SEE ADDITIONAL NOTES IN SPEC FOR A REFERENCE IMAGE
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Too Many Erroneous Runs] 
At least 3 runs were not successfully completed (resulted in an Error).
Fewer than 3 runs were not successfully completed (resulted in an Error).
